question: Who appoints the Attorney General of India?
solution:
The correct answer is__** President.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 76 has provided for the office of the AGI.
 
• Appointed by **President.**__
 
• AGI must be a person who is qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• AGI must be a citizen of India and he must have been a judge of some high court for 5 years or an advocate of some high court for 10 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The **power **of Attorney General is **he gives advice to the government of India **upon such legal matters, which are referred or assigned to him by the President and he represents such other duties of a legal character that are referred or assigned to him by** the President.**
 
• **Impeachment:- **Procedures and grounds for the removal of** AGI** are not stated in the Constitution. She/he holds office during the contentment of the President.
 
 
• AGI may be removed by the** President** at **any time**.
